summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting, found to have severe metabolic acidosis due to acute on chronic renal allograft dysfunction. She required intubation for refractory acidemia, which was complicated by aspiration and subsequent septic shock. She developed ARDS, was managed with lung-protective ventilation, and improved with broad-spectrum antibiotics after E. coli was isolated from sputum. A new atrial fibrillation was treated with amiodarone, and anticoagulation with warfarin was initiated despite a recent GI bleed, after shared decision-making. An ischemic stroke was identified on CT, likely due to hypotension, with no lasting deficits. Right thigh abscesses were drained multiple times, with fluid collections consistent with lymphoceles. Renal allograft failure led to initiation of hemodialysis, and a tunneled catheter was placed. She stabilized, was extubated, weaned off pressors, and discharged home with services for IV antibiotics, dialysis, and wound care.
